methods_quotes.q: Data were weighted to be nationally representative.
Statistical software was used to compute 95% confidence intervals for prevalence estimates.
Differences in tobacco use estimates during 2002--2004 were assessed by using t-tests at two-tailed significance level.
All statistically significant results were p<0.05.
significance testing did not control for possible changes in demographics from 2002 to 2004.
